slot_note: Redraw in a new world: the seed FC48 world (drop-off recycling bins) died at stage 1 on measurement before any card; its screens are in task177/DESIGN_NOTE.md Tried and rejected.
niche: a provincial employment service's forecast of the share of jobseekers' own contacts its upgraded digital assistant takes in the eight weeks after an assistant-first period, from each claimant's contact-by-contact channel choices and the outcomes they met
analyst_test: A strong analyst who stitches each claimant's call legs and assistant conversations into contacts, reads the seven-day resolution rule and the routing codes correctly, fits a reinforcement-learning model of channel choice with one learning rate to every contact, checks it on held-out contacts and simulates the eight assistant-first weeks files an assistant share of about 33 per cent of claimants' own contacts for March and April, where the share is about 22 per cent.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is how far a contact the jobseeker did not choose moves their later channel choices against one they chose, estimated the way computational behavioural modelling estimates learning (a reinforcement-learning model of each claimant's contact-by-contact choices fitted by likelihood, compared out of sample and simulated forward); with machines' routing tables or another field's tallies in place of jobseekers the agency term has nothing to act on and the task stops making sense.
layer1: the contact-centre platform's interaction-leg export: one row per leg (IVR entry, queue, transfer, adviser answer, callback), several legs to one call, timestamps in UTC
the digital assistant's conversation export in local time, a conversation that times out and is reopened split into several sessions, the entry route (app, web, IVR transfer) on each
the telephony platform replaced mid-2026: leg codes and column names change, a crosswalk issued

claimants keyed by case number in the case system, by phone number in telephony and by account ID in the assistant, joined through a contact-details crosswalk with changed numbers and shared household phones
resolution never recorded: derived from no repeat contact on the same topic within seven days, topics recoded when the topic list was revised
queue overflow episodes logged by the workforce team per queue and interval, separately from the legs
staff and test accounts in the assistant export, advisers using the assistant on a claimant's behalf
claims opened and closed through the year (people finding work), the planning population defined on the register date
stakeholder_role: behavioural insights adviser in the service's digital channels team

spine.entity: one leg of a jobseeker's call through the contact-centre platform (IVR entry, queue, transfer to the assistant, adviser answer, callback)
spine.source: synthetic (constructed in the layout of a contact-centre platform's interaction-leg export)

world.org_type: provincial employment and income assistance service (fictional)

driver: Experiences a unit did not choose move its later choices far less than experiences it chose, so a period that sends every unit to one option converts few of them; the record holds those imposed experiences only as scattered single episodes, so a learner fitted to the whole record with one rate over-predicts the conversion, and only a separate rate for the imposed experiences, read from those episodes, carries to the period.
driver_concrete: Jobseekers sent to the digital assistant when the phone queue overflows learn about a fifth as much from it as those who open it themselves, so the eight assistant-first weeks, which send every call to the assistant, lift claimants' own use of it in March and April far less than a reinforcement-learning model with one learning rate predicts.
stump: One learning rate fitted to every contact and simulated through the assistant-first weeks files about 33 per cent of claimants' own contacts in the assistant for March and April; the overflow-redirected contacts in the record teach about a fifth as much as chosen ones, so the share is about 22 per cent.

differentiation.task70: task70 rebuilds a per-record date with a class-conditional cut from an event log under a filed clause; here no record date or filed clause decides: a learning rate for contacts the claimant did not choose is estimated inside a reinforcement-learning model and simulated through a window of such contacts.
differentiation.task104: task104 replays a self-adapting scorer at a setting it never ran, masked by its own reference window; here the units are people learning from outcomes, and the decisive quantity is how far an experience they did not choose updates them, read from scattered overflow redirects.
differentiation.task134: task134's yield is a rebuild chance gated by an option's value against a cost step; here nothing is gated or stepped: the forecast is a learning process whose update from imposed contacts is about a fifth of the update from chosen ones.
differentiation.task168: task168 completes capped units' demand from a same-month build; here no unit is capped or censored: imposed experiences move choice values less than chosen ones, and a window made of them converts few units.
differentiation.task463: task463 weights price comparisons around cut periods in a chained index; here the decisive step is a learning model's update rate for experiences the unit did not choose, simulated forward through eight weeks of them.
differentiation.task501: task501 rebuilds a static who-passes-to-whom matrix from the days of the season's own regime; here the regime-only static rebuild (next-contact transitions after redirected contacts alone) misses by about a fifth, because imposed experiences accumulate through learning, so the forecast needs the imposed-contact learning rate inside a jointly fitted reinforcement-learning model.
